title: Soft-start prober and fractional kernel activation for v3 adoption
creator: Anya Patel
description: Problem: Directly switching a large fraction of decode/prefill work to FlashAttention v3 on multi-tenant nodes triggers startup latency spikes, memory fragmentation, and occasional OOMs during warmup windows. These regressions appear stochastic across model families and sequence-length distributions. Goal: implement a lightweight, runtime-side "soft-start prober" that enables fractional activation of v3 kernels per-GPU and per-model fingerprint, ramping usage gradually while collecting warmup telemetry and enforcing SLO-safe thresholds. The feature should be reversible and runnable without model changes, support staged rollouts, and require minimal scheduler changes.
acceptance_criteria: (1) v3 activation can be limited to an adjustable fraction (0-100%) per node and per model-fingerprint. (2) Rolling activation shows no >5% increase in 95th percentile decode latency or >0.5% increase in error rate at the cluster level compared to baseline. (3) Telemetry exposes kernel_switch_ratio, v3_warmup_latency_ms, kv_cache_miss_rate_during_warmup. (4) Automated rollback triggers when thresholds exceeded and completes within 2 minutes. (5) E2E canary run against a synthetic mix (short chat, long context, embeddings) validates safety before production rollout.
plan_steps: Design an in-runtime gating layer that samples requests and routes a configurable fraction to v3 kernels (fractional activation).
Add a small prober that, on a per-model-fingerprint basis, performs warmup decodes/prefill sequences to populate KV cache and stabilize workspace allocations.
Emit telemetry events: kernel_attempted, kernel_accepted, kernel_fallback_reason, v3_warmup_complete, v3_warmup_latency_ms, prefill_kv_hits.
Add safety circuit: SLO guardrails (p95 latency increase, error rate, OOM count) and soft throttle that reduces v3 fraction on breach.
Implement canary orchestration scripts to run fractional activations across pods in stages (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with automated checks.
Create dashboard and alerting on new metrics and integrate into rollout job.
experiments: Experiment A: Fractional activation only — compare steady-state latency at fractions {1,5,20,50}. Measure p50/p95/p99 for decode and prefill.
Experiment B: Prober enabled — run warmup prefills before routing live traffic and measure reduction in p95 and kv_cache_miss_rate.
Experiment C: Multi-tenancy stress — enable fractional v3 on nodes with mixed model families (Llama-2-like, mix of short/long contexts) to measure memory fragmentation and OOM incidence.
Experiment D: Sequence-length mixing — synthetic workload with 8/128/2048 token requests to verify kernel selection stability during bursts.
telemetry_queries: kernel_switch_ratio = sum(kernel_attempted == v3 and kernel_accepted)/sum(kernel_attempted) by node, model_fingerprint
oom_incidents_during_warmup = count(oom) where context = 'warmup' group by node
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Local developer testing on dev cluster with synthetic workloads. Verify basic correctness.
Stage 1 (Canary): 1% traffic to v3 fraction across dedicated canary nodes for 1h. Automated checks: p95 latency delta < 3%, error delta < 0.2%, no OOMs.
Stage 2: 5% fraction for 2h after passing canary. Verify kv_cache_miss_rate < baseline + 2%.
Stage 3: 20% fraction for 4h with multi-tenant stress workload. If stable, proceed.
Stage 4: 50% then 100% gradual increases with continuous monitoring; each stage requires green automated checks before advancing.
rollback_criteria: p95 latency increases > 5% over baseline for >10 minutes
error rate increases > 1% absolute for >5 minutes
>= 1 OOM per node in a 15-minute window attributed to kernel activation
